1, - Definitions; County - shall refer to Treutlen County, Georgia, which includes all property within the limits of the county. , Commissioners - shall refer to and mean the Commissioners of Treutlen County, Georgia.

; / Clerk ~ shall refer to the Clerk, Assistant Clerk, or Deputy Clerk appointed by the Commissioners. Beer - shall mean beverages made in whole or in 1 part from malt or any similar fermented beverage containing not more than 6% of alcohol by volume. Manager - shall mean the person or persons in charge of day-to-day operations of the business establishment for which application is being made and whose primary place of employment is at said location. Premises - shall refer to the area enclosed by the building in which the licensee is operating a business,
1: No beer, malt beverages as defined herein, shall be sold in the county except under a license granted by the Commissioners.
2:
Licenses required under this Article are hereby classified as follows:

- (a) Retail beer - packaged (not to be consumed on premises).

- (bo) Retail beer - consumption on premises, This type will not be issued to any licensee where beer is to be sold on the premises in connection with the operation of any other public business, except the operation of a cafe or restuarant (not to include drive-in eating establishments). Consumption on the premises is not allowed in any other instances.
3: All applications for a license, under this Article, except for transfer of existing licenses, shall be accompanied by cash or certified check in the amount prescribed in the license and tax ordinance and for the classifications within which the license falls. All applications shall be made by the manager or managers upon a form to be supplied to all applicants by the Deputy Clerk. If the business establishment is not open and no manager or managers has been designated at the time the application is made, the application may be made by any person, but, if a license is issued under these circumstances, the license must be transferred to the manager or managers prior to the making of any sales of beer. The forms supplied to the applicants by the Deputy Clerk shall contain the following information which may be supplemented by any information requested by and in the discretion of the Commissioners. That the applicant has not been convicted of any felony or maintaining a house of prostitution and has not been within the last five years of the date of the application convicted of a violation of any laws regarding the use, sale or possession of alcoholic beverages.
4:
All applications shall also contain an oath providing that the information disclosed in the application is true and correct and providing further that each applicant will abide by, observe, and conduct the business according to the ordinances of the County, the laws of the State of Georgia, and the rules and regulations of the State Department of Revenue in respect thereto. Each applicant shall sign said oath in the presence of the Deputy

Clerk who shall witness the same.

The following procedure shall be followed with respect to each new application for the issuance of a license under this

Article which is filed with the Deputy Clerk:

(a)

(b)

At the time of filing such application, the applicant shall deposit with the Deputy Clerk cash or certified check in the amount determined by the Deputy Clerk as sufficient to pay the cost of processing the application. This deposit shall not be refunded, either in whole or in part, to the applicant unless the application is withdrawn prior to the same being processed. Promptly upon the filing of each such application, the Deputy Clerk shall refer the same to the Sheriff for investigation and recommendation to the Commissioners. The Sheriff shall attach his written recommendation to the application and return to the Deputy Clerk at least five days prior to the meeting at which the application is to be considered. In the event the Sheriff shall be unable to complete his investigation and make his recommendation within the time prescribed, a written statement setting forth the reasons for the delay shall be attached to the application and delivered to the Deputy Clerk. AS soon as the reason for the delay has ceased to exist, the Sheriff shall give written notice to the Deputy Clerk who shall mark the same "Filed" and the date thereof. Upon receiving such notice from the Sheriff, the Deputy Clerk shall treat the applica- tion as if newly filed and proceed to comply with the

provisions of this section.

- (c) Petitions for and against the granting of a license under this ARticle shall be accepted by the Deputy Clerk for filing until such time as the Commissioners have either granted or denied the license applied for.

- (a) The Commissioners may deny a license under this Article for any of the following reasons:

- (1) The applicant or any of applicant's employees at the proposed location has been convicted of a felony or of a violation of the laws or regulations of any State or political subdivision relating to the use or sale of drugs or alcoholic beverages.. The forfeiture of a bond or collateral or a plea of nolo contendre shall be considered a conviction of the purpose of this Section.

- (2) The making of any false statement on an application for a license under this article.

- (3) The applicant is determined to be a front for any person whose license has been revoked or who is not eligible for a license under this article.

- (4) The proposed location is a "trouble spot" in the judgment of the Commissioners by reason of disturbances or acts of disorderly conduct, violence, or gambling, having occurred in said location or on the premises thereof.

- (5) The existence of dangerous traffic conditions at the proposed location or a determination by the Commissioners that the granting of a license would cause dangerous traffic conditions.

- (6) A determination by the Commissioners that the granting of the license would adversely affect the neighborhood or cause a substantial diminution and value of the immediate adjacent and surrounding property.

- (7) There are license fees or advalorem taxes owed

The prospective transferee shall file with the Deputy Clerk an application for transfer which shall contain the same information and require the same oath as set forth in Sec. 4 and Sec. 5 hereof. Said application for transfer shall be accompanied by cash or certified check in the amount of the transfer fee as prescribed from time to time by resolution of the Commissioners. Promptly upon the filing of an application for transfer the Deputy Clerk shall mark same "Filed" and the date thereof and refer the same to the Sheriff for investigation and recommendation to the Commissioners. The Sheriff shall file his written recommendation with the Deputy Clerk at the earliest possible time and upon receipt thereof the Deputy Clerk shall place the application for transfer on the agenda for the next regular scheduled meeting of the Commissioners who shall approve or disapprove the same.

In the event a licensed establishment is closed, the licensee must surrender the license to the Deputy

(grounds for suspension or revocation)

The making of any statement on an application for a license under this Article, which is later found to be false, shall be grounds for suspension or revocation of such license as has been issued pursuant to said application.
12:
No person under the age of 18 years may apply for a license under this Article nor may any employee under the age of 18 years engage in the sale of beer.

Sec, 14. - Violations and Penalties:

The performance of any act prohibited by any section or provision of this Article, or the failure to perform any act required thereby, shall constitute a violation of this Article and an offense hereunder and any person found guilty of a viola~ tion of any section or provision of this Article shall be subject to having his license suspended or terminated.
13:
- (a) Any license issued under this Article may be suspended for a definite time or may be revoked if the licensee or any employee of the licensed establishment has been convicted of the violation of any act prohibited by this Article or of failure to perform any act required by this Article or is convicted of the violation of any state or federal law relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages or drugs. The forfeiture of a bond or collateral or a plea of nolo contendre shall be considered a conviction for the purposes of this section. __

(b)

Any license issued under this Article may be suspended for a definite time or revoked if the Commissioners have determined that there is probable cause to believe that the licensee or an employee of the licensed establishment has violated a State or Federal law relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages or drugs. The procedure for making such determination shall - be;

at

- (1) The Sheriff, after obtaining reliable information that such violation has been committed, shall cite the licensee to appear for a hearing on a day certain before the Commissioners and shall advise the licensee of the law believed to have been violated.

- (2) The Commissioners, after hearing evidence, shall Make a determination whether there is probable cause to believe the alleged violation has been committed.

If the hearing results in a determination that probable cause does exist, the findings shall be reduced to writing and filed with the Deputy Clerk.
14: No licenses issued under this Article May be suspended or revoked unless the licensee has been afforded the opportunity for a hearing before the Commissioners. The licensee shall be given at least five days written notice delivered to the licensee in person or by United States Certified Mail of the time, place, and purpose of the hearing and the grounds for suspension or revocation. At such hearing the licensee shall have the right to appear}: in person or by attorney and have witnesses appear on his behalf.
15:
Upon adoption of this Article and the Signing thereof by the Commissioners same shall become effective and all ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict are hereby repealed.
